# Run Page Lineage and Result First

The task page shows how each run followed the one before it. Open a run to see what it produced and what needs your attention before opening its record or conversation.

## What It Does

The **Runs of this task** rail starts with the oldest run. Each connection names why the next run exists, such as **Tried again with your guidance**, **Re-run after your review**, **Ran again exactly**, or **Repaired with AI**. When the next run has a recorded reason, the connection quotes a one-line excerpt of up to 140 characters. The full guidance or review feedback remains in **How this run was made**. Each run shows its number, state, and age. A run used to create a saved-task revision has a **Saved as** link; a task started from a saved task shows its origin before Run 1.

A run page reads in this order:

1. The run number, state, connection, duration, and one cost total when the provider reported a cost. **Show technical details** appears here.
2. Any current action, such as answering a question, approving a run, or reviewing its result.
3. **Result**: available output files, the final **Answer** for a completed text-only run, or one outcome summary with next steps. Partial outputs remain visible when a run fails. A completed run also offers **Save this task**.
4. **How this run was made**, closed initially, with the run state and input and output counts in its heading.
5. **Conversation**, open during an unfinished run and closed after it ends.

**What you asked** appears once on the task page. Record sections keep their titles separate from their summaries. For the details behind file previews and downloads, see [Results, Outputs, and Downloads](results-outputs-downloads.md); for the saved-task flow, see [Save and Rerun](save-and-rerun.md).

An unsuccessful run has one outcome summary explaining the recorded cause and offering relevant next steps. A failed check can link to **Checks** in the run record; generation failures can list the failed attempts; an interrupted run is distinguished from a run you cancelled. The latest settled run has one **Run again** control in its outcome, with optional guidance. A saved-code run offers **Run again exactly** and **Repair with AI** there. While a run waits for your result review, **Did this do what you wanted?** is the retry path. An earlier run links to the later run that came from it. A completed run without an outcome summary puts its retry control under **Run it again** in **Result**. See [Execution History](execution-history.md) for retry consent and recovery behavior.

## How to Use It

Open a task from **History** at `/history`, or go directly to `/tasks/{taskId}` for its latest run. Select a numbered node in the rail to open `/tasks/{taskId}/runs/{executionId}`. The rail scrolls sideways when long and stacks vertically on a narrow screen. Select **Show earlier runs** at the start of the rail to load older entries.

Read **Result** first. Expand **How this run was made** for the saved inputs, guidance, checks, decisions, and run details. Expand **Conversation** for the transcript, or select **Open the transcript** from a next step. Use **Show technical details** in the run header to reveal tool calls and timings, turn and token counts, runtime preparation, raw failure lines, and diagnostic codes. Turning it off hides those display details without removing saved events or other conversation messages.

## Inputs and Outputs

The rail reads the paged `GET /api/tasks/{taskId}/runs` response. Each item includes a `reason` excerpt or `null` and a `savedAs` array containing saved-task IDs, names, and revision numbers. The rail displays the runs loaded so far in oldest-first order; the API pages are newest first. The run record retains the full person-supplied words. These fields add to the existing history response; they do not change how a run starts.

The **Result** section uses the run's saved events, output list, and outcome details. Output files keep their existing preview and download controls. The header shows cost only when the provider reported it; the switch reveals token counts only when those figures were reported.

## Configuration and Permissions

**Show technical details** starts off and is saved per browser under `automate.showTechnicalDetails`; a change in another tab follows into this one. If browser storage is unavailable, the run page still works with technical details off. There is no feature-specific server setting or account role. Retrying follows the existing disclosure review and run permissions described in [Execution History](execution-history.md).

## Limitations

- The rail shows runs within this task. A **Saved as** marker links to the saved task, but runs in other tasks that later used that revision are not drawn here.
- A connection quotes only a shortened reason. Open **How this run was made** for the full recorded words.
- Provider cost and usage figures appear only if the provider reported them.
- An earlier run does not offer another retry while a later run exists; follow its link to the later run.
